en.title: Split Points Where Sorting Both Parts Yields a Sorted Array
en.description:
Split the array into a non-empty front part and a non-empty back part, sort each in ascending order, and concatenate them in their original order. Count the cut points where the concatenated result is non-decreasing.

The standard input/output format was compiled by CSWork; value ranges marked "this site" are this site's judging conventions.
en.input: The first line contains n (2..100000), and the second line contains n integers (1..10⁹).
en.output: Output the answer required by the problem.
en.explanation: Example 1: cutting after 1 or after 2 is valid, 2 in total. Example 2: only the cut between 2 and 10 is valid, 1 in total. Example 3: both cut points allow equal values at the boundary, 2 in total.
hints: Precompute the minimum of every suffix and scan the prefix maximum; a cut point is valid when prefix maximum≤suffix minimum.
